content: MySQL, which I'm using for Daytona, has the idea of relevance in searches. Previously I had been showing results in reverse chronologic order. So now, a search for Matt Mullenweg gets the same results but prioritized by MySQL. This is the query. What's nice is that the results are focused on the early 2000s, when the standards we use now were coming up. We can do this kind of stuff again. There's more to do. For example, it would be really cool if Pocket Casts, their excellent podcast client, would let a user publish their subscription list so we can build applications on it. There's a whole new base of data to work with. And unlike other media, podcast content is meant to be shared. The controversies that exist for professional writing and audiobooks, for example, don't seem to apply to podcasts, with the caveat that I am not a lawyer. If we could open this up, we could create an ecosystem worth of applications very quickly. OPML is an easy format to ingest into a database. FeedLand for example, does some wonderful things with OPML. We just need sources of interesting data. Today it's locked up in the podcast clients.
